
[3] rewrite

```
**The release check, and why it allows 0.5%.** The model advances in fixed
steps of 0.1 s, and a shorter step should give almost the same result. Before
each release, a test reruns the first minute of the default sevoflurane
induction with steps of 0.1 s, 0.05 s and 0.025 s. Each run's alveolar,
vessel-rich and mixed-venous concentrations must be within 0.5% of the run with
the next shorter step. A compartment that holds almost no agent also passes if
its two values differ by less than 0.000001 vol%, because there a tiny
difference is a large percentage. The 0.5% was set for the simulator's earlier
calculation method, at about ten times the 0.04% alveolar difference that the
method showed. On 2026-10-03, the current method's runs agreed to better than
one part in a trillion, so the much tighter limits in the paragraphs above are
the ones that would catch a real error.
```

[4] rewrite

```
The 5e-3 relative tolerance was chosen when the simulator used an earlier,
approximate method (the operator split). That method showed a relative gap of
4e-4 in the alveolar fraction between steps of 0.1 s and 0.025 s, and 5e-3 is
about ten times that gap. With the current method (the exact step), the same
comparison gave relative gaps of about 1.4e-13 on 2026-10-03, so the tolerance
is kept as a coarse check. For a fraction so close to zero that a relative gap
means little, the 1e-8 absolute tolerance lets a negligible difference pass.
```

[5] rewrite

```
**The release check, and why it allows 0.5%.** The simulator moves the model
forward in fixed time steps, normally 0.1 s long. A shorter step should give
almost the same result. If it does not, the step is too long. Before each
release, the check runs the first minute of the default sevoflurane induction
three times, with steps of 0.1 s, 0.05 s and 0.025 s. In each run, the
alveolar, vessel-rich and mixed-venous concentrations must be within 0.5% of
the run with the next shorter step. In a compartment that still holds almost
no agent, a tiny difference can be a large percentage, so a percentage means
little. Two values for such a compartment also pass if they differ by less
than 0.000001 vol%, which is one part in a hundred million of the gas.

The 0.5% margin was set for the simulator's earlier calculation method. With
that method, the alveolar concentrations of the 0.1 s and 0.025 s runs differed
by about 0.04%, so the margin allowed about ten times that difference. The
check compares each run only with the next shorter step. Under the earlier
method, a direct comparison of the 0.1 s run with the 0.025 s run would have
failed, because their mixed-venous concentrations differed by 0.55%. At one
minute, those concentrations have barely begun to rise. On 2026-10-03, the
current method's three runs agreed to better than one part in a trillion.
The check is therefore now only a coarse safety net. The much tighter limit in
the paragraphs above the release check is the one that would catch a real error.
```
